title: Provisioning deconfliction and capacity commitment windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers need a clear, auditable process for requesting reserved GPU capacity that guarantees throughput for committed windows while enabling autoscaling and temporary bursts. Current intake forms and approval flows are fragmented across spreadsheet approvals and ad-hoc Slack threads. This causes deconfliction (double-booked pools), slow approvals for high-throughput customers, and billing/proration ambiguity for partial-month commitments.

Goal:
- Design and ship a provisioning workflow that: (1) prevents reservation conflicts across teams and regions, (2) supports multiple commitment window types (sustained commit, short burst, test/POC), (3) exposes throughput guarantees in the approval matrix, and (4) integrates with autoscaling policies and fleet controls so customers get the promised latency/throughput SLOs.

Scope (this ticket):
- Intake form redesign with explicit throughput SLA fields (tokens/s, sustained RPS, p95 latency target).
- Approval matrix UX that surfaces: available pool capacity, existing reservations (read-only), estimated headroom after allocation, and billing proration for partial windows.
- Define internal rules to deconflict overlapping requests (first-commit wins for sustained windows; burst buckets for short windows subject to remaining burst quota).
- Hook to autoscaling policy templates so reservations can bind to an autoscaling profile (min, target, max GPUs; coldstart buffer).
- Audit trail + notification: create events for request, approve, reject, amend; include links to provisioning runbooks and capacity run dashboards.
- Acceptance criteria and telemetry: reservation success rate, time-to-approve median, number of deconflict incidents, billing proration accuracy.

Non-goals (this ticket):
- Low-level orchestration changes to the runtime (handled by ENG sub-issues).
- Billing engine redesign beyond proration calculation and labels.

Proposed workflow (high level):
1) Customer/SE/AE fills intake form (UI + API): fields include desired start/end, throughput profile, expected steady-state tokens/s, burst allowances, region, and preferred autoscaling profile.
2) System performs soft validation: checks model compatibility, quota, and theoretical throughput given requested GPUs. If theoretical capacity is insufficient, offer model/quantization suggestions.
3) Reservation tentative hold: system places a 72-hour tentative hold and marks impacted pools as "pending" for the requested window. The hold reserves capacity for planning but does not bill until approved.
4) Approval routing: automated routing based on request size and SLA tier: 
   - <= 2 GPUs: Auto-approve if headroom exists and no overlap with sustained commits.
   - 3-16 GPUs: Requires capacity planning reviewer approval (capacity planner team).
   - >16 GPUs or long sustained windows (>90 days): Escalation to product ops + finance for pricing and contract.
5) Deconfliction policy: for overlapping holds, prioritize existing sustained commitments; tentative holds that conflict are flagged in the UI with suggested alternatives (shift window, reduce throughput, apply burst profile).
6) On approval: system converts hold to committed reservation, triggers allocation runs to pin/prepare fleet (warm KV caches if needed) and binds the reservation to the chosen autoscaling profile. Billing begins per proration rules.
7) During active window: autoscaling policies maintain SLOs; metrics feed into the console showing real-time utilization, throttle events, and forecasted headroom.
8) End-of-window: optional automatic renew prompt with renewal recommendations based on observed utilization and QoE.

Edge cases and decisions to make:
- Tentative hold duration: default 72 hours but configurable per-org. Decision: adopt 72h for now.
- Overcommit strategy: allow temporary overcommit for burst windows if aggregate utilization falls below threshold for last 7 days. Requires explicit customer opt-in.
- Billing for aborted reservations: define cancellation window to avoid abuse; propose full refund if canceled >14 days before start, 50% if within 14-3 days, no refund within 72 hours.

Acceptance criteria (deliverables):
- UI prototype for intake and approval routing (Design approved)
- API endpoint for creating tentative holds and converting to commits (ENG PR merged)
- Approval rules implemented in orchestration service (ENG config + tests)
- Autoscaling profile binding implemented and verified in staging (SRE sign-off)
- Dashboard panels showing reservation state, conflicts, and key telemetry (console-2026.04)
- Documentation: runbook for capacity planners, customer-facing KB article on commitment types, and billing proration doc.

Telemetry & Dashboards to implement:
- Reservation lifecycle: created -> hold -> approved -> active -> expired/canceled (count & median times)
- Headroom after allocation (per pool)
- Number of conflict events and time-to-resolution
- SLO attainment for committed reservations (p95 latency, tokens/s achieved vs committed)
- Billing proration audit logs

Open questions / Risks:
- Legal/Finance need to sign off on cancellation/refund policy (blocking for release).
- Autoscaling profiles may need additional runtime hooks to guarantee warm-start latency—ENG dependency ENG-3017.
- UX for showing "suggested alternatives" needs design iteration to avoid surfacing sensitive capacity data between customers in shared pools.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Reservation+Lifecycle+Proposal
- Design mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd-reservation-ux
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5602 (tentative hold API)
- Capacity dashboard (staging): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/reservations-staging

Next steps:
- Schedule 30m sync with Capacity planners + Eng infra (Mar 15) to align on hold semantics and autoscaling hooks.
- Design: deliver high-fidelity intake and approval screens by Mar 19.
- Engineering: break down ENG work and create sub-issues for API, orchestration, and billing proration by Mar 18.

Owner notes:
- Prioritize auditability and clear UX language to reduce back-and-forth with Sales/Finance.
- Keep initial release conservative: no cross-customer capacity transparency beyond what is needed for planning suggestions.
